nodes.name: ingest typed alert payload
nodes.notes: SKELETON. Normalise the inbound alert into the SecOps-NG alert envelope. Two source shapes are required by the roadmap acceptance criteria (push from detection pipeline, pull from a shared alert store); the dispatcher branches on __alert_source_shape__. Body of the normalization rules lands in the CORE-INGEST card.

nodes.name: enrich with telemetry context

parameters.pythonCode:
from alert_triage.primitives.suppression import canonical_seen_key
__seen_key__ = canonical_seen_key(asset_ref=__asset_ref__, classification=__classification__, detection_rule_id=__detection_rule_id__, subject_ref=__subject_ref__)

nodes.notes: SKELETON. Pull adjacent telemetry for the entities named in the alert (subject identity, source/destination, asset) so the prioritisation policy and suppression check have evidence beyond the alert envelope itself. Stubbed; the enrichment fan-out lands in CORE-ENRICH.

nodes.name: suppress and close
nodes.notes: SKELETON. Link this alert onto the existing case (or onto the benign-rule record), close it without paging, and account the suppression against the false-positive-rate KPI and (when the suppression covers a re-fire of a previously closed case) the recurring-incident correlator.

nodes.name: classify and prioritise (deterministic policy)
nodes.notes: SKELETON. Apply the operator's prioritisation policy. The policy itself is expressed as code (the roadmap pins this: deterministic prioritisation, DSPy used only for free-text fields like the analyst summary). Output is __priority__ ∈ {p1_severe, p2_high, p3_routine, p4_informational}.

nodes.name: response: p1 severe — page and escalate
nodes.notes: SKELETON. Page the on-call responder, open the incident case, stamp the timeline-start signal, and hand off to the incident management playbook. Records against the MTTR-critical clock and the regulator-notification-overrun KRI window.

nodes.name: response: p2 high — queue for primary analyst
nodes.notes: SKELETON. Queue the case to the primary analyst queue with the enriched evidence packet, no page. Records against the MTTR clock and the handoff-brief delivery SLA.

nodes.name: response: p3 routine — queue for review
nodes.notes: SKELETON. Append to the review queue for batched analyst attention; no SLA clock beyond the routine review-completion SLA.

nodes.name: response: p4 informational — log and close
nodes.notes: SKELETON. Record the alert for telemetry-coverage accounting and close without further action. Feeds the false-positive-rate denominator and the detection-coverage view.

nodes.name: already-seen or known-benign?
nodes.notes: Suppression branch. on_success: matches a known-benign rule or an already-seen case fingerprint inside the window; suppress and close. on_failure: proceed to prioritisation.

values.name: __alert_id__
values.description: Identifier of the inbound alert in the operator's alert store. Carried opaquely; the source shape is asserted in __alert_source_shape__.

values.name: __alert_source_shape__
values.description: One of: push_detection_pipeline, pull_alert_store. Used to select the normalization path in the ingest step.

values.name: __benign_or_seen__
values.description: Set by the suppression check: true when the alert matches a known- benign rule or an already-seen case fingerprint inside the configured suppression window.

values.name: __priority__
values.description: Deterministic priority assigned by the prioritisation policy. One of: p1_severe, p2_high, p3_routine, p4_informational.

nodes.name: route on priority
nodes.notes: Route to the response branch keyed on the deterministic priority. Each branch is a single response-routing action that hands off to the appropriate downstream playbook or owner queue. Bodies of downstream playbooks are out of scope here.
